annotations.keyFindings: In 146 trials the median absolute improvement was 4.3 percentage points (interquartile range 0.5 to 16); larger effects with low baseline, repeated feedback, explicit targets and action plans.
annotations.limitations: Feedback design poorly described; few patient outcomes or unintended effects reported.

annotations.keyFindings: Practices given a printable overdue list improved by 9 percentage points against 2 in practices with the same dashboard without the list, over nine months in 12 plus 12 practices.
annotations.limitations: Allocation by practice preference; higher baseline in comparison practices.

annotations.keyFindings: Peer comparison raised monitoring completion by 3.1 percentage points (95 percent confidence interval 0.9 to 5.3), mostly in the lowest third of practices at baseline.
annotations.limitations: Staff found comparisons with dissimilar practices unfair.

annotations.keyFindings: Log-ins fell by 71 percent within three months in 58 practices; views of patient-level lists, not summary charts, preceded improvement.
annotations.limitations: Logs cannot show what staff did after viewing.

annotations.keyFindings: Among 6,420 people, 18 percent of ordered urine albumin tests and 6 percent of ordered eGFR tests were not completed within three months.
annotations.limitations: One record system; reasons for non-completion unknown.

annotations.keyFindings: Duplicate kidney testing within 30 days of a hospital test rose from 5 to 11 percent after feedback began, among 3,115 patients also seen in hospital clinics.
Later-starting practices can serve as concurrent comparisons if the schedule is unrelated to performance; adjust for baseline and check pre-rollout trends.

claims.text: Across 146 trials of audit and feedback, the median absolute improvement in compliance with desired practice was 4.3 percentage points.
claims.passage: The median absolute improvement in compliance with desired practice was 4.3 percentage points (interquartile range 0.5 to 16).
claims.interpretation: Sets a realistic expectation for any dashboard effect: a few percentage points.

claims.text: Practices given a printable list of overdue patients improved monitoring by 9 percentage points against 2 in practices with the same dashboard but no list.
claims.passage: the proportion of patients up to date with monitoring rose by 9 percentage points in practices given the list and by 2 percentage points in comparison practices
claims.interpretation: The patient list is the feature most likely to matter.

claims.text: In primary care records, 18 percent of ordered urine albumin tests were not completed within three months.
claims.passage: In total, 18 percent of ordered urine albumin tests were not completed within three months, compared with 6 percent of ordered eGFR tests.
claims.interpretation: The outcome must be completed tests, not orders.

claims.text: Dashboard log-ins fell by 71 percent within three months of launch.
claims.passage: Log-ins fell by 71 percent within three months of launch.
claims.interpretation: Feature use should be measured from the logs over time.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Audit and feedback yields small average improvements (median 4.3 percentage points), larger with low baselines, repeated feedback, targets and action plans. A controlled before-after study and usage logs point to patient-level lists as the feature that turns feedback into action, and peer comparison adds a few points in low performers. Ordered tests overstate completion, especially for urine albumin, and feedback can increase duplicate testing. A staggered rollout can be evaluated with later practices as concurrent comparisons if the schedule is unrelated to performance. The five discovery leads, including one presented as a landmark trial, are unchecked and are not appraised here.
gradeRationale: One review of randomised trials and one cluster trial support small effects of feedback in general; the evidence on patient lists is a single non-randomised comparison; outcome and overtesting evidence is observational.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; four source-derived claims; overall certainty low.
